events.what: Caltech Math-AI Lab preprint gives new record determinant lower bounds (explicit matrices) at orders 51, 107, 111, 115, 119
events.ai_basis: The findings presented in this work grew out of research conducted at the Caltech Math–AI Lab, whose mission is to develop new AI systems and algorithms capable of performing effectively in sparse–reward, long-horizon environments. (plus, per the record, the lab site credits this result to its 'RL-based solvers for combinatorial challenges')

events.what: Maximal determinants over l-th roots of unity

judgement.doubts: F3/F9: record lower bounds at five orders are a table advance (bound), not a determination of any order, so progress is right. The AI role rests on a thin paper quote (F9 names this exact case) supplemented by the lab website's attribution of the result to RL solvers, which the researcher paraphrased; the methods section was never read. If the paper describes a human-designed classical search, the role would drop to assisted or none.

corrections.why: F9: kept with doubt. ai.basis_quote only names the lab's mission and does not say who found the matrices; the `generated` code leans on the record's paraphrase that the lab site credits this Hadamard result to its 'RL-based solvers', and the record's `incomplete` admits the methods section was not read.
